<ticket source="">
# # The app is slow on big lists

- Ticket: request
- State: open

## Description

# The app is slow on big lists

**Type:** bug, performance

> From Camille, operations:
>
> Our "Warehouse" list is past 10,000 tasks now and the page takes ages to show it. Sometimes it just spins and
> the browser asks whether to stop the page. Changing the sort or picking a tag is just as slow, and so is opening
> the list on a phone. Smaller lists are fine. Can someone have a look? We will only get more tasks.

Reproduced on a copy of their data: `GET /api/lists/:id/tasks` on a list of 10,000 tasks takes 2 to 3 seconds on a
quiet developer machine and up to 9 on a busy one, and answers all 10,000 tasks in one response; the page then
renders every one of them.

## Expected

1. Opening a list, changing its sort or its filters is fast whatever the size of the list.
2. The tasks of a list come in pages (see the API notes). The order, the filters and the fields of each task stay
   as the README documents them.
3. The page follows: it shows the first page and loads the next ones on demand.
4. Tests cover paging; the README documents it.

## API notes

`GET /api/lists/:id/tasks` takes two more parameters, `limit` (1 to 200, default 50) and `cursor`, on top of the
existing filters and sorts, and answers `{"items": [<task>, …], "next_cursor": "<opaque string>" | null}` instead of
an array: this changes the shape of the response, and the page must follow. `next_cursor` is `null` on the last page;
otherwise, passed back as `cursor` with the same filters and sort, it answers the next page. A cursor only works with
the list and the sort it came from: any other `cursor` answers `400`.
</ticket>

plan.summary:
Big lists are slow for three reasons: the tasks endpoint returns every task at once, it runs three extra queries per task (tags, comment count, assignee), and the tasks, task_tags and comments tables have no useful indexes. The page then builds every row. The plan has three tasks and no open questions.

1. Back end (T1). `GET /api/lists/:id/tasks` takes `limit` (1 to 200, default 50) and `cursor`, and answers `{items, next_cursor}`.
- The cursor is a keyset cursor, not an offset: an opaque base64url JSON holding the list id, the sort and the last row's sort key values. Ties are broken by id.
- Each of the four sorts (position, due_date with nulls last, priority, created) gets a comparison that matches its ORDER BY exactly.
- Cursor values reach SQL only as bound parameters. A malformed, forged, wrong-list or wrong-sort cursor, or a `limit` outside 1..200, answers 400.
- The query fetches limit+1 rows to decide `next_cursor`.
- The per-task queries are replaced by batch queries for the whole page. `toView` becomes a batch builder that `getTask`, `viewOf` and `updateTask` also use.
- A new migration is appended to `src/db.ts`; no shipped one is edited. It adds one index per sort, shaped like that sort's ORDER BY and starting with list_id. It also adds task_tags(task_id), task_tags(tag_id, task_id) and comments(task_id).
- T1 also updates `test/tasks.test.ts` for the new shape and adds paging tests.
- T1 owns the README section, so no separate docs task is needed.

2. Page (T2). `public/tasks.js` reads `items` and `next_cursor`. It shows the first page and adds a "Load more" button that appends the next page. The button reuses the existing button styles and is hidden when `next_cursor` is null. Changing the sort, a filter or the list resets to page one. Responses that arrive late after such a change are ignored.

3. QA (T3). It checks every criterion, including paging across all four sorts with duplicate keys, null due dates and filters. It also checks the 400 cases, that no page repeats or skips a task, and that no query runs per task. It adds any missing regression tests.

T1 and T2 run in parallel against the contract written in both goals. The `tasks` fields stay as the README documents them.

acceptance.text: Opening a list, changing its sort or its filters on a list of 10,000 tasks returns only one page (default 50) and no longer scales with list size; the page no longer runs per-task queries for tags, comment count or assignee.

GET /api/lists/:id/tasks accepts limit (1 to 200, default 50) and cursor, and answers {"items": [task...], "next_cursor": string|null}; next_cursor is null on the last page. Order, filters (done, tag, assignee), sorts and task fields are unchanged from the README.

Following next_cursor with the same list, filters and sort visits every matching task exactly once, in the documented order, for all four sorts (position, due_date with null dates last, priority, created), including tasks that share a sort key.

A malformed, forged, tampered, wrong-list or wrong-sort cursor answers 400, as does a limit that is not a whole number from 1 to 200; the cursor never reaches SQL as text and access control still goes through loadList.
A new migration (a new entry in src/db.ts, no shipped one edited) adds indexes supporting the four sorts per list and the tag and comment lookups, and applies cleanly on an existing database.

The page shows the first page, offers a Load more control that appends the next page while next_cursor is non-null, resets to the first page when the list, sort or filters change, and keeps working for edits (done, title, tags, delete, comments).

Tests cover paging (limit, cursor, last page, each sort, ties, null due dates, filters, invalid cursor and limit) and the full test suite passes; the README documents limit, cursor, the response shape and the 400 rules.

out_of_scope: Offset or page-number pagination, and a total count in the response
Infinite scroll or virtualised rendering on the page (a Load more button only)
Paging of other endpoints (activity, comments, tags, lists)
Changing sorts, filters, task fields or authentication
Changing or renumbering existing positions (known issue in the README)
Binding the cursor to the filters (the ticket only binds it to the list and the sort)

tasks.goal:
Page the tasks endpoint, batch the per-task queries, add the index migration and document it.

1) src/tasks.ts, listTasks(db, user, listId, query): return `{ items: TaskView[], next_cursor: string | null }`. src/app.ts line 75 needs no change since `ok(...)` serialises whatever listTasks returns; touch it only if needed. Keep loadList first for access control. Keep the filters (done, tag, assignee) and SORTS unchanged.
- `limit`: absent = 50; otherwise it must match /^[1-9][0-9]*$/ and be <= 200, else badRequest (400). `limit=0`, `-1`, `abc`, `1.5`, `201` all answer 400.
- `cursor`: opaque base64url of JSON `{ l: listId, s: sort, k: [...] }`, where k holds the last returned row's sort key values. position: [position, id]. due_date: [due_date|null, id]. priority: [priority, id]. created: [created_at, id]. Parse defensively: any decode, JSON or type failure, a wrong list id, a sort different from the request's, or k with the wrong length or types (integers, string or null as the sort expects) answers badRequest('invalid cursor'). Never put cursor text in SQL; use `?` bound parameters only. The ORDER BY keys come from the fixed SORTS map.
- Keyset comparison must match each sort's ORDER BY exactly, with a strict 'after the cursor row' condition ANDed to the existing filters: position: (t.position, t.id) > (?, ?). priority: priority < ? OR (priority = ? AND id > ?). created: created_at < ? OR (created_at = ? AND id < ?). due_date (ORDER BY due_date IS NULL, due_date, id): if cursor due_date is null then due_date IS NULL AND id > ?; else due_date > ? OR (due_date = ? AND id > ?) OR due_date IS NULL.
- Fetch limit+1 rows; if there are more, drop the extra and build next_cursor from the last kept row, else null.

2) Remove the per-task queries. Replace toView(db, task) with a batch builder (e.g. `toViews(db, tasks: Task[]): TaskView[]`) that runs, for the ids of the page, one query for tags (`task_tags` JOIN `tags` WHERE task_id IN (...), ordered by name), one for comment counts (GROUP BY task_id) and one for assignees (`users` WHERE id IN (...)). Chunk the ids if more than 200 are passed. Make getTask, viewOf and updateTask use it with a single-element array. The TaskView shape and field values stay exactly as they are, including tags sorted by name, comment_count 0 when none and assignee null when unset.

3) src/db.ts: append ONE new entry at the end of `migrations` (never edit a shipped one; adding to the end bumps user_version). Use CREATE INDEX statements, with IF NOT EXISTS being optional. Indexes: tasks(list_id, position, id); tasks(list_id, due_date IS NULL, due_date, id) as an expression index; tasks(list_id, priority DESC, id); tasks(list_id, created_at DESC, id DESC); task_tags(task_id, tag_id); task_tags(tag_id, task_id); comments(task_id). Check with EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN that each sort's query uses its index with no temp B-tree for ORDER BY, and mention what you saw in the report. The dba reviews this migration.

4) test/tasks.test.ts (and test/helpers.ts if needed): update existing tests that read the array to read `.items`, and add paging tests through the HTTP server as the file already does: default limit 50 and limit boundaries; limit and cursor 400 cases (limit 0, 201, abc; garbage cursor; cursor from another list; cursor from another sort; hand-forged base64 JSON with wrong types); a walk over every page for each of the four sorts with 120+ tasks, with shared positions, shared priorities, identical created_at and a mix of null and set due dates, checking each task appears exactly once and the order equals the unpaged order; next_cursor null on the last page and on an empty list; filters (done, tag, assignee) combined with paging; and a test that the tags, comment_count and assignee on a page are right. Also add a migration test that an existing database at the previous version upgrades.

5) README.md: in the Tasks section, update the `GET /api/lists/:id/tasks` row and the paragraph below it to document `limit` (1 to 200, default 50), `cursor`, the `{items, next_cursor}` response, that next_cursor is null on the last page, that the cursor is opaque, only valid with the same list and sort (and should be sent with the same filters), and the 400 cases. Add a line to Layout or Known issues only if relevant. Keep the existing wording style.

Contract with T2: `GET /api/lists/:id/tasks?sort=&done=&tag=&assignee=&limit=&cursor=` answers 200 `{"items": [<task>, ...], "next_cursor": "<opaque string>" | null}`. Each task has the same fields as today. T2 passes next_cursor back unchanged as `cursor` with the same list, sort and filters. Nothing else in the repo calls listTasks. Run `npm test` before finishing.

Make the page follow the paged tasks API. Contract with T1: `GET /api/lists/:id/tasks?sort=...&done=...&tag=...&limit=&cursor=` now answers `{ "items": [<task>, ...], "next_cursor": "<opaque string>" | null }` instead of an array. The first request sends no cursor (the default limit of 50 is fine, `limit` may be omitted). To load more, send the same list, sort and filters plus `cursor=<next_cursor>` unchanged, as an opaque string; next_cursor null means no more pages. The cursor works only with its own list and sort, otherwise the API answers 400.

In public/tasks.js, renderTasks(): read `items` and `next_cursor`, replace the list with the first page, and keep the cursor in module state. Add a 'Load more' button after the `#tasks` list (add it to public/index.html next to the list, `hidden` by default) that fetches the next page with the current sort and filters, appends the new items (reuse taskItem) and updates or clears the cursor; hide it when next_cursor is null. Reuse the existing `button` styles and the element helpers; add CSS in public/style.css only if the control needs spacing, and keep it usable on a phone width (full width or a 44px-high target is fine). Disable the button while a page is loading, show errors with showError, and give it a native button element with a visible focus state. After loading more, keep keyboard focus on the button, or on the first new item if the button disappears. Reset to page one (new request without cursor, clear the old cursor) whenever the list, sort, done filter or tag filter changes, and after any refresh() that re-renders the list. Ignore responses that arrive after the list or filters changed (for example with a request counter) so a late page never gets appended to the wrong view. Do not change how items look or the other actions (done checkbox, title edit, tags, comments, delete). Do not touch src/ or README.md (T1 owns them). Check by running the app (`npm start`) against a list with more than 50 tasks if you can; otherwise read the code through carefully, and report which.

Check every acceptance criterion with evidence once T1 and T2 are merged, and add the missing regression tests. Run `npm test` and report the result. Seed a database with a list of 10,000 tasks (with tags, comments and assignees, and with repeated priorities, equal created_at values and null due dates) and measure the first page for each sort, with a tag filter and with a done filter, against the pre-change behaviour in the ticket (2 to 3 seconds); confirm with EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN that each sort and the tag and comment lookups use the new indexes. Walk all pages of each sort and check that each task appears exactly once and the order equals the README's order. Check the 400 cases: invalid or truncated cursor, cursor of another list or another sort, forged cursor with wrong types or an SQL-looking string, limit 0, 201, abc. Check that a list owned by another user still answers 404, with or without a cursor. Check that the page shows 50 tasks, that Load more appends and then disappears at the end, and that changing sort, filter or list resets it. Check that README matches the real behaviour. Add tests only for gaps you find, in test/tasks.test.ts (do not rewrite T1's tests); report what failed, with the command and output, rather than fixing source files outside tests.

routing.reason: Performance bug on large lists: the tasks endpoint returns everything with several queries per task and has no index on tasks, and the fix is keyset pagination across four sorts, a changed response shape, a small page change, a new index migration and docs.
rulings: Ruling: default workflow, M — the work crosses API, a DB migration, the page and the README, but it is one well-specified change — cost if wrong: a gate step the work did not need.
Ruling: skip `frame` (po) — the ticket already lists testable acceptance criteria and the API contract — cost if wrong: an edge case in the cursor rules goes unframed; the plan must cover it.

Ruling: no architect, no UX, no PM, no SEO — keyset paging fits the existing design in src/tasks.ts, and the page keeps its layout and gets a 'load more' control; the lead should reuse the existing button and element styles — cost if wrong: an inconsistent control to fix in review.

Ruling: keep `migrations` (dba review) active — the real cause includes no index on tasks(list_id, …) and per-task queries for tags, comments and assignee; an index migration must be a new entry in src/db.ts, never an edit of a shipped one — cost if wrong: a slow query that survives the paging.

Ruling: the plan should also remove the per-task queries in `toView` (batch the tags, comment counts and assignees of a page) — paging alone leaves up to 200 x 3 queries per page and the ticket asks for speed on every list change — cost if wrong: the list stays slower than needed.

Ruling: keyset (not offset) cursor bound to list id and sort, tie-broken by id, with the SORTS' null handling for due_date; a malformed, forged or foreign cursor, and `limit` out of 1..200, answer 400 — cost if wrong: duplicated or skipped tasks across pages.

Ruling: security effort medium — the cursor is user-controlled input parsed server-side (must never reach SQL as text; use bound parameters only) and access control stays through loadList — cost if wrong: a missed injection or cross-list read; low enough since queries are bound.

Ruling: the response shape change is the ticket's explicit decision, so the page (public/tasks.js) must follow in the same run and `next_cursor` must be consumed by a 'load more' on demand; no other client of `listTasks` exists in the repo — cost if wrong: a broken page between merges.
Ruling: budget $3 — covers the plan, the implementation (back and page), review rounds, security and dba reviews — cost if wrong: the run stops before the final reviews.

question.question: Who fixes the Load more button staying visible on the last page, a one-line rule `#load-more[hidden] { display: none; }` in public/style.css?
question.why: The only failing check comes from this CSS rule. The file belongs to the page task (T2), not the back end, and the checks cannot pass until it is fixed.
options: The page owner (T2's role) fixes it
The back end adds the one-line rule
proposed: The page owner (T2's role) fixes it
implications: Keeps each role on its own files; the run needs a page fix step before the checks can pass.
Fastest, and the change is tiny, but the back end edits a file outside its scope.

answer: The page owner (T2's role) fixes it

reviews.summary:
One bug blocks shipping: the "Load more" button stays visible on the last page, and `npm test` fails. The back end looks correct.

What I checked:
- I read the whole diff against the base and ran `npm test`. It ran 49 tests: 47 pass, 1 is skipped (it was skipped before) and 1 fails, as T1 and T3 reported.
- The failing test is test/tasks.test.ts:481, the check that `#load-more` has a `[hidden]` guard.
- I did not run a browser or re-measure 10,000-task timings. I did not re-run T3's EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN or seeding checks, or the 400 cases by hand.

Back end (src/tasks.ts, src/db.ts):
- Each sort's cursor condition matches its ORDER BY, including due_date with nulls last and the id tie-break. For created, both the date and the id run descending.
- Cursor values are bound parameters.
- The cursor is checked for shape, size and type, and for list and sort. `loadList` still runs first.
- `limit` is validated by regex and range. The keyset query fetches limit+1 rows.
- `toViews` batches tags, comment counts and assignees in chunks of 200.
- The migration is a new entry at the end of `src/db.ts`. It has one index per sort plus the tag and comment indexes. No shipped migration was edited.
- The README documents `limit`, `cursor`, the response shape and the 400 rules.

Page (public/tasks.js): the first page replaces the list and Load more appends. A request counter drops late responses, and changing sort, filter or list resets to page one. Nothing in the diff goes beyond the ticket.

The bug (AC6):
- `public/style.css:46` sets `#load-more { display: block; … }`. An ID rule beats the browser's built-in `[hidden]` rule, so the button shows even when `next_cursor` is null. That is every list under 50 tasks, and the last page of any list.
- The user decided that the page owner (T2) fixes it. T1 and T3 correctly left it alone, and no task has fixed it yet.

Minor points I did not raise as findings: `refresh()` after an edit collapses the loaded pages back to page one, and a failed first request leaves the button hidden. Neither breaks a criterion.

findings.scenario: Open any list with fewer than 50 tasks, or scroll to the last page of a bigger one. The response has next_cursor null, so tasks.js sets loadMore.hidden = true. `#load-more { display: block }` overrides the browser's [hidden] rule, so the button is still shown and clicking it does nothing. This breaks AC6 (Load more disappears at the end), and the T3 regression test at test/tasks.test.ts:481 fails, so `npm test` fails (AC7).
findings.fix: Add `#load-more[hidden] { display: none; }` to public/style.css, or drop the `display: block` declaration. Then `npm test` must pass.

Earlier finding F1, "Load more" staying visible on the last page, is fixed. `public/style.css:47` now has `#load-more[hidden] { display: none; }`. The regression test at test/tasks.test.ts:481 now passes, so AC6 and AC7 hold.

Page (`public/tasks.js`) in this round:

- After an edit, `refresh()` reloads page one and collapses any pages already loaded.

report.summary:
AC6 FAILS because of one front-end bug; AC1–AC5 and AC7 PASS (AC7 with CONCERNS, since the new test below fails). `npm test` ran 49 tests: 47 pass, 1 skipped (it was skipped before) and 1 fails. The failing test is my regression test for the bug.

THE BUG (AC6): `public/style.css:46` sets `#load-more { display: block; … }`. An ID rule beats the browser's built-in `[hidden]{display:none}`, so "Load more" stays visible when next_cursor is null (the last page, and a list under 50 tasks). Clicking it does nothing. The fix is `#load-more[hidden]{display:none}`, or dropping the `display` declaration. I did not fix it, because source files are outside my remit. I found this by reading the CSS and did not run it in a browser. The test asserts that the stylesheet has the guard, and it fails today.

PASS:
- AC1: I seeded 10,000 tasks with tags, comments, assignees, ties and null due dates. A first page took 0.2–0.7 ms for each sort, with a tag filter and with a done filter, against 2–3 s before. Each page ran 4–5 prepared statements, however large the page (my new test checks this).
- EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN: each sort searches its own index (tasks_list_position, tasks_list_due_date, tasks_list_priority, tasks_list_created). The tag lookup uses task_tags_task, and comments use comments_task. No temp B-tree appeared.
- AC2/AC3: walking all pages of each sort at limit 200 visited all 10,000 tasks once each, in the README order. My new tests walk 600 heavily tied tasks with limits 1, 13 and 200.
- AC4: T1's tests cover the 25 bad cursors and the bad limits, and a stranger's list answers 404, with or without a cursor. Cursor values are bound `?` parameters. I did not re-run the limit cases by hand.
- AC5: the new migration is the last entry in `src/db.ts` and applies on a version-6 database (T1's test).
- AC7: the README matches the behaviour.

Mutation checks: I reversed the created tie-break, and 4 tests failed, including my tie test. I made `toViews` run per task, and my query-count test failed.

CONCERNS (code reading only, no browser run):
- After an edit, `refresh()` goes through `renderLists`, which reloads page one. Pages already loaded collapse.
- A failed first-page request leaves the button hidden.

affected_views.state: last page or list under 50 tasks: Load more should be hidden (it is visible)

out_of_scope_findings: BUG to fix in public/style.css:46: `#load-more{display:block}` defeats the `hidden` attribute, so Load more shows on the last page. Add `#load-more[hidden]{display:none}`. test/tasks.test.ts ('the Load more button is hidden…') fails until then.
After any edit, delete or comment, refresh() reloads page one, so pages already loaded are lost and the user's scroll position is lost with them.

report.summary:
No vulnerabilities confirmed in this diff. I checked by reading the code and did not run the app or `npm audit`.

Checked, no finding:
- Cursor input (A05:2025): `decodeCursor` in `src/tasks.ts` limits the length to 512 and the characters to base64url. It requires the list id and sort in the cursor to match the request, and it type-checks the key and id per sort. `afterCursor` passes every cursor value to SQL as a bound `?`. The `limit` value is a bound parameter too, and it must be a whole number from 1 to 200 or the API answers 400. The interpolated parts (`SORTS[sort]`, the `IN (?,…)` placeholder lists) are not user text, and `sort` is validated with `Object.hasOwn`.
- Access control (A01:2025): `loadList` still runs first in `listTasks`, so another user's list answers 404 with or without a cursor. The cursor is unsigned, but forging one only moves the starting point inside a list the caller already owns. It reaches no other list, and it cannot reach another sort because the sort is part of the cursor.
- Batch queries: `toViews` selects tags, comment counts and assignees only for the task ids it was given. The assignee is a username the caller could already see through those tasks, and `getTask`, `viewOf` and `updateTask` keep their existing access checks.
- Errors (A10:2025): Malformed JSON in a cursor, or base64 that decodes to garbage, is caught and answers 400. It does not fall through to an unbounded query.
- Page (`public/tasks.js`, A05:2025): No new `innerHTML` use. The new code only consumes `items` and `next_cursor`. A request counter drops late responses after a list, sort or filter change.
- Migration (`src/db.ts`): A new final entry that only creates indexes. No shipped migration was edited and there is no data change.
- Dependencies (A03:2025): `package.json` and the lockfile are unchanged, so there are no new or updated packages.
- Abuse cases (A06:2025): A single request is capped at 200 rows plus one, and the `IN` lists are chunked at 200, which is under SQLite's variable limit. This reduces the cost of one request compared with the old unbounded endpoint.

Not covered:
- I did not run the test suite, `npm audit` or the app.
- I did not review authentication, the other endpoints, or code outside the diff.

Candidates: none.
out_of_scope_findings: The cursor is not bound to the filters, so a cursor reused with different filters just gives different results. The ticket excludes this, and it is not a security issue.
